title: chat-v1-stream-graft-priority-stop-logprob-annotations-toolcall-delimiter
author: Evelyn Morgan
description: Context: Customers reported inconsistent behavior between Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer and upstream OpenAI semantics when (1) multiple stop sequences overlap with token boundaries, (2) logprobs are requested together with function/tool calling metadata, and (3) framed streaming envelopes interleave toolcall boundary tokens. Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI compatibility surface with expected client behavior so that integrations relying on stop precedence, logprob provenance, and function-call boundaries do not observe regressions during streaming or when using fallback model variants. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) Stop reconciliation: Introduce a deterministic priority policy for overlapping stop sequences (longest-match first, then earliest-occurring) and ensure the stream terminates with a stop fragment that preserves the exact byte offsets clients expect. 2) Logprob annotations: When clients request logprobs alongside function/tool calls, annotate returned logprobs with provenance tags ("response", "toolcall-prefix", "toolcall-output") so downstream scorers can attribute token probabilities properly. Keep the extra metadata compact to avoid adding per-token payload overhead for clients that do not request logprobs. 3) Toolcall delimiter stabilization: Add an explicit framed delimiter event in the streaming envelope to mark toolcall handoff points; this reduces race conditions where partial tool outputs would be emitted inline with model tokens. Changes in this PR: - server/api/openai_compat/chat_adapter.py: Adds stop reconciliation module and config flag to enable longest-match policy; wire-up for streaming envelope delimiter. - server/stream/framer.py: New envelope type "TOOL_DELIM" and deterministic emission ordering to avoid interleaved fragments. - runtime/proto/logprob.proto: Extend logprob message with a provenance field (enum) and compact bitflags. - runtime/handlers/chat_stream_handler.go: Integrate provenance wiring so logprob requests flow end-to-end during streaming. - docs/openai_compat.md: Expanded compatibility notes and a migration section explaining the stop priority semantics and the new logprob provenance field. - tests/test_chat_stream.py: Add integration tests covering overlapping stops, logprob+toolcall scenarios, and streaming boundary events. Summary of commits: - 1a2b3c4: initial implementation of stop reconciliation logic and unit tests - 2b3c4d5: add streaming envelope TOOL_DELIM and framer changes - 3c4d5e6: wire logprob provenance through proto and handler path - 4d5e6f7: docs, test harness updates, and CI flake fixes Testing and CI: The first CI run showed a flaky streaming test (test_toolcall_boundary) on macOS runners; I adjusted test timing and rewrote the harness to use deterministic pseudo-clock. After two reruns all checks passed (build, unit, integration, linters). Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind feature flag "compat.stream_graft_v1" default-on for canary clusters. We'll monitor the per-route regression dashboard for 72 hours, focusing on end-to-end test sets (Linear ENG-8421) and customer reports. Backwards compatibility: The new stop priority is opt-in via config for older Dedicated/Private installations — the hosted API will use the new behavior to match upstream expectations. Release notes: "OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: deterministic stop matching, logprob provenance, and stable toolcall streaming delimiter (backward-compatible opt-in for self-hosted)."
